summary: Exit polls project a major victory for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, with 44-44.5% of the vote. This far exceeds the conservative CDU's 18.5%, though it remains uncertain whether the AfD will secure enough seats to govern. No far-right party has won control of a German state since World War Two.
key_points: Exit polls project the AfD to win 44-44.5% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt.
The conservative CDU is projected to finish second with 18.5% of the vote.
The AfD views the result as a historic outcome and claims a mandate to govern.
Whether the AfD can take power may depend on which smaller parties pass the 5% threshold.

title: US envoys Kushner and Witkoff arrive in Kyiv after talks with Putin
author: Amy Hawkins
content:
The US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Kyiv for a second day of talks on how to end the war in Ukraine.
Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, met the pair in Sophia Square, in front of Kyiv’s historic Saint Sophia Cathedral. Zelenskyy greeted Witkoff with a hug, saying: “It’s good to see you, Steve.”
The cathedral is a few hundred metres away from the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU intelligence agency, which was hit by a Russian drone on Friday afternoon, marking an escalation in a conflict that has now dragged on for more than four and a half years.
![Steve Witkoff goes to embrace Volodymyr Zelenskyy as security personnel look on](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/10961d7e2853e24c784f689e27165ce35210227b/1367_1026_5275_4220/master/5275.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Witkoff and Kushner are meeting Zelenskyy the day after holding three hours of talks in Moscow with Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin.
The US envoys have visited Russia several times, but this is their first visit to Ukraine. The trip is intended to mark an intensification of efforts to end the war in Ukraine, although details of any peace proposal remain unclear.
British, French and German national security advisers were reportedly in Kyiv on Sunday before the arrival of Witkoff and Kushner.
Talks between Russia and Ukraine on ending the war have focused on a 20-point peace plan put forward by Washington and Kyiv in December. But the two sides have failed to reach common ground on several sticking points, including control of territory in east Ukraine.
A White House official said on Saturday that the talks with Moscow “discussed substantive plans for next steps” for ending the war and said an announcement would follow in the coming weeks.
The senior Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the talks as “extremely frank” and said there was an acknowledgement of the need to address “the root causes of the conflict”.
![Vladimir Putin shakes hands with Jared Kushner as Witkoff looks on](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/353bd0bc9e5a6513ebdd2c741ee76f2d4f130399/0_0_3342_2547/master/3342.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Moscow and Kyiv pledged to refrain from strikes on each other’s capital cities for three days to ensure the smooth passage of the negotiators. Zelenskyy said on Sunday that the plans for the US envoys to fly into Moscow had been upended by Russian strikes on Kyiv’s two main airports on Friday evening.
Ukrainian airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Other visiting dignitaries have travelled overland by train from neighbouring countries.
Kyiv and the surrounding areas have been hit by a barrage of daily drone strikes for more than a week, the most sustained attack on Ukraine’s capital in months.
after newsletter promotion
The capital is now enjoying a reprieve from strikes and air raid alerts that had become a daily occurrence, but other parts of the country are still being hit. Ukrainian authorities reported on Sunday that at least eight people were killed and 69 injured across Ukraine in the past day.
Ukraine is facing a critical shortage of US-made Patriot interceptor missiles that can shoot down incoming threats. Many of the recent Russian strikes have been by new-model jet-powered drones that can reach speeds of 250mph, making them hard to intercept.
Many Ukrainians are worried about the war dragging on into a fifth year and are anxious about the winter ahead. This week, Zelenskyy’s defence technology adviser, Serhii Beskrestnov, told the Guardian that the government should consider evacuating elderly people from Kyiv as Putin had ordered the Russian military to “prepare and carry out mass strikes” on Ukraine’s energy facilities.
Russia and Ukraine have increased their use of long-range missiles in recent weeks in an effort to sap morale in each other’s countries.
Additional research by Illia Dyadik
summary: US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Kyiv for discussions with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy following three hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. The visit marks the US envoys' first trip to Ukraine as part of intensified efforts to end the ongoing war. Current negotiations center on a 20-point peace plan, though significant sticking points remain regarding territorial control and root conflict causes.
key_points: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Kyiv for their first visit to Ukraine following talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met the US negotiators in Sophia Square in Kyiv.
Talks to end the war have focused on a 20-point peace plan put forward by Washington and Kyiv in December.
Discussions have faced obstacles, with both sides failing to reach common ground on sticking points such as control of territory in east Ukraine.

title: US military says it struck three Iranian tankers after American warships came under missile attack
author: Marina Dunbar
content:
The US military said Saturday it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US navy warships came under missile attack, further escalating tensions in the region and warning it would “if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet”.
According to the military, a US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks” while patrolling the region. No US personnel were injured.
Two of the Iranian oil carriers were “permanently disabled”, the Pentagon said, while a third tanker, which was unladen, was destroyed.
The US said the vessels were part of a shadow network that helped finance Iran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards and armed proxy groups operating across the region.
“We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet,” the head of US Central Command, Adm Brad Cooper, said in the statement.
The announcement followed an earlier report from Iran that the US had attacked an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island in the Gulf. Tasnim, a semiofficial news outlet affiliated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, reported the strike happened on Saturday morning. It said the tanker’s crew survived and was being evacuated.
The US said one tanker was struck off Kharg Island, while another was hit near Jask. The unladen tanker was struck in the Gulf of Oman. The US statement also shared what it described as video footage of the strikes.
Iran’s state broadcaster said later Sunday that Iran targeted three oil tankers and three American vessels in response to the US strikes. This could not be immediately confirmed.
The latest attacks came nearly a week after the US and Iran resumed strikes after about a month of relative calm in the on-again, off-again war that began with US and Israeli attacks in February. Attempts at negotiations have collapsed.
One of the strikes hit a wedding in southern Iran on Tuesday, killing four people, including a child, and injuring dozens, according to Iranian officials.
after newsletter promotion
The US vice-president, JD Vance, said “sometimes things happen” when asked on Thursday whether an US strike was responsible for killing people at the wedding celebration.
The renewed strikes have also brought fresh scrutiny to a 28 February US attack in Minab that struck a school compound and killed at least 156 people, most of them schoolchildren.
A preliminary US military inquiry reportedly found that the attack resulted from a targeting error after outdated coordinates identified the school as part of a nearby Revolutionary Guards naval base. The Pentagon said at the time that it was investigating. A full report has not been made public.
Associated Press contributed reporting
summary: The US military stated it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US warships avoided unprovoked missile attacks in the region. The Pentagon reported that two tankers were permanently disabled and a third was destroyed, noting the vessels helped finance Iran's Revolutionary Guards and proxy groups. Meanwhile, Iranian state media reported that Iran targeted three oil tankers and three American vessels in response. The renewed hostilities follow recent high-casualty incidents, including a strike on a wedding and a February attack on a school compound in Minab.
key_points: The US military struck three Iranian oil tankers following missile attacks on US warships.
The Pentagon stated two tankers were permanently disabled and a third was destroyed.
The US identified the targeted vessels as part of a network financing Iran's Revolutionary Guards and proxies.
Iranian state media reported that Iran targeted three oil tankers and three American vessels in retaliation.
Recent escalations follow prior deadly incidents, including strikes that hit a wedding and a school compound.

title: Russia-Ukraine war: US envoys set for Ukraine talks after Putin meeting
author: Toby Mann
content:
![Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff wait before a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin in Moscow, Russia](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/f8dc/live/731248d0-a997-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
US envoys Jared Kushner (left) and Steve Witkoff
- Published
Two US envoys are hoping for "equally productive meetings" in Ukraine after holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on ending the war, US officials say.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to land in Kyiv on Sunday, having "discussed substantive plans for next steps" with Putin on Saturday, according to the White House.
It is not yet clear exactly what they are, but an announcement is expected in the coming weeks, as efforts to end the war in Ukraine gather pace.
It will be to the first trip by US President Donald Trump's top negotiators to Ukraine's capital. Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days.
Watch: President Putin welcomes US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to talks in Moscow
As Witkoff and Kushner were negotiating at the Kremlin, Zelensky said he was ready for "a substantive conversation".
Saturday's talks in Moscow lasted three hours and were held behind closed doors in Putin's official residence in the heart of the Russian capital, according to Russian state media.
Details are still emerging, but both sides have given broadly positive remarks without going into specifics.
Putin adviser Yuri Ushakov described the talks as "constructive, extremely frank".
"The talks were not limited to an exchange of views on resolving the Ukrainian crisis - economic issues and potential major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects were discussed in considerable detail," he said.
Ushakov also said "note was made of the Russian army's tangible advances in the combat zone" and that there was acknowledgement that talks needed to address "the root causes of the conflict".
Despite an escalation of Russian missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian cities including Kyiv, Russian ground forces have made very slow advances for most of the conflict, incurring enormous casualties. Russia still controls about one-fifth of Ukrainian territory - areas that it seized back in 2022.
Kushner and Witkoff have visited Russia several times but given Ukraine's airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, it is not clear how they will be travelling to Kyiv from Moscow.
The talks come after Russia and Ukraine have intensified aerial attacks in recent months.
Ukraine says it has struggled to repel ballistic missile attacks due to a lack of interceptor missiles, while Kyiv has focused its strikes on Russian economic infrastructure targets, notably oil installations.
summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are scheduled to travel to Kyiv for meetings in Ukraine following a three-hour closed-door discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow regarding efforts to end the war. White House officials stated that substantive plans for next steps were discussed during the Moscow meeting, with an announcement expected in the coming weeks. Meanwhile, Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have agreed to temporarily halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days.
key_points: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
The envoys are set to arrive in Kyiv on Sunday for their first trip to Ukraine's capital.
Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days.
Details of the Moscow talks remain limited, but Russian adviser Yuri Ushakov described them as constructive and frank.

title: Paris drops Mercator projection: France now looks smaller on world maps
author: Alexander Kazakevich
content:
France is redrawing its world map: deeming the Mercator projection misleading, the foreign ministry will drop it in favour of a map that better reflects actual continental sizes, especially Africa.
A shrunken Africa, a Greenland and a northern Russia that seem to stretch into infinity: that is about to disappear from the maps used by French diplomacy.
Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced on Friday that his department is abandoning the so-called Mercator projection, which artificially enlarges polar regions and visually downplays the size of equatorial areas. France will now use instead the Eckert IV projection, which reflects the true proportions of the continents more accurately.
As a result, France will appear smaller on the map compared with countries close to the equator, just like the United States or Russia.
'A map is never entirely neutral'
In a speech at the Sorbonne university during the public event "La Fabrique de la diplomatie" or "The making of diplomacy", the French minister said that "the time has come" to "correct" how the world is perceived through maps inherited from 16th-century Western navigators.
In a speech delivered at the Sorbonne for the public event "La Fabrique de la diplomatie", the French minister said that "the time has come" to "correct" how the world is perceived through maps inherited from 16th-century Western navigators.
"A map is never entirely neutral. Take the Mercator projection, the one every one of us has known since childhood. The areas we see on it do not correspond to actual areas: (...) The United States, Russia, China take on a disproportionate visual importance compared with Africa, Latin America or South-East Asia," the French foreign minister said.
Jean-Noël Barrot also cited the example of Greenland, which is roughly the same size as the Democratic Republic of Congo or Algeria, even though it "seems almost as vast" as the entire African continent.
"Changing the map obviously does not change the world. But correcting a representation that distorts it is already an act of truth," he stressed.
The ministry began reducing its use of the Mercator projection in 2021
Meanwhile, French diplomatic maps will not change overnight but the process is already underway, Euronews has learned from a diplomatic source. The ministry began reducing its use of the Mercator projection in 2021, "with the aim of providing a more accurate geographical representation of the world."
The projection has been "gradually phased out" across all public diplomacy websites, the source said.
"The advantages and biases associated with each type of representation are presented at various events attended by the ministry's cartographers," the Quai d'Orsay added, citing the European Heritage Days and the International Geography Festival in Saint-Dié-des-Vosges.
"France will continue this work, prioritising map projections suited to different purposes and providing a more accurate reflection of geographical realities in its diplomatic communications."
French diplomats nevertheless acknowledge that the Mercator projection remains relevant "in a limited number of cases", including regional or local uses around the equatorial zone, as well as for navigation charts.
At the UN, a cartographic victory for Africa
The announcement in Paris comes as, in New York, the world map is also being redrawn. A few hours later, the United Nations General Assembly officially abandoned the Mercator projection in favour of a projection based on the Equal Earth model, created in 2018 and closer to the real proportions of the continents.
The non-binding resolution, entitled "Correcting the map"and sponsored by Togo, was backed by 164 member states. The African Union had already adopted Equal Earth in March, and the text now encourages countries to do the same.
Only the United States voted against, denouncing what it called a "radical ideological project", notably because of a passage in the resolution stating that "correcting cartographic distortions relating to the size of continents constitutes an act of cognitive justice and memorial reparation".
Six countries – Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine – abstained.
The UN stresses that the resolution does not ban the Mercator projection, "nor does it impose a single map". The resolution "encourages governments, educational institutions, international organisations and technology companies to make use of the Equal Earth projection, or of other so-called 'equal-area' maps that preserve the true proportions of surface areas.
France has therefore joined this movement, but has opted to adopt the Eckert IV projection, created in 1906. It is similar to the Equal Earth projection recommended by the UN, though not identical. Both represent the size of the continents much more faithfully than the Mercator projection, but they differ slightly in the shapes they give to the landmasses.
As the UN points out, Mercator mapping will not disappear altogether. Digital platforms such as Google Maps also currently use a version of this projection.
In French schools, most world maps are still in Mercator. "You can find Eckert or Peters* in some textbooks, but that is very rare," says Grégory, a senior history and geography teacher in Rennes, speaking to Euronews.
It remains to be seen whether the maps used in schools will also follow the shift launched by the foreign ministry.
*another equal-area projection, which provides a better representation of the continents' true surface area – Euronews.
Read more
![A piece of the Hellenic Air Force F-4 Phantom fighter jet is visible at its crash site at Tanagra air base.](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/90/25/95/480x270_cmsv2_b372487a-7ccd-5a7e-8c56-be1a28bf8974-9902595.jpg) 
![Foreign Ministry](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/90/23/43/480x270_cmsv2_04a42231-05ff-5154-8bb2-a860d58695f0-9902343.jpg) 
![FILE - A boy cycles past a cooling towers of a coal-fired power plant in Dadong, Shanxi province, China, 3 Dec. 2009.](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/90/12/08/480x270_cmsv2_f4dd6bb4-336b-56aa-b990-8116f6956043-9901208.jpg)
summary: The French foreign ministry is abandoning the Mercator map projection in favor of the Eckert IV projection to better reflect the true sizes of continents, particularly in equatorial regions and Africa. This decision aligns with a broader international shift, as the United Nations General Assembly also recently voted to adopt the Equal Earth projection. While the French ministry began phasing out Mercator maps in 2021, the projection remains widely used in schools and digital navigation tools.
key_points: France's foreign ministry is replacing the Mercator projection with the Eckert IV projection for diplomatic communications.
The Mercator projection is being dropped because it artificially enlarges polar regions and downplays the size of equatorial areas like Africa.
The United Nations General Assembly recently adopted a non-binding resolution encouraging the use of the Equal Earth projection to preserve true surface proportions.
The United States voted against the UN resolution, calling it a radical ideological project.
Mercator maps will still be used in specific contexts, such as local navigation charts and digital platforms like Google Maps.

title: Putin begins talks with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on ending war with Ukraine
author: William Christou
content:
Russian president Vladimir Putin began talks with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on ending more than four years of war in Ukraine in the Kremlin Saturday, ahead of their first visit to Kyiv expected on Sunday.
Both Russia and Ukraine vowed not to strike each other’s capitals for three days during the negotiations, as Washington tries to revive US-led talks to end Europe’s worst conflict since the second world war.
The visit came as Donald Trump suggested on Friday a new proposal to end the war, without providing any details on what his new plan might be. Trump made ending the war a priority early in his second term, but his efforts have so far yielded little results.
Trump said his son-in-law Kushner and business ally Witkoff were bringing “a proposal to end the war”.
“Dear colleagues, I warmly welcome you to Moscow. The situation is, of course, not simple,” Putin told the envoys in a grand Kremlin hall in footage aired by Russian TV. “But before we begin to address it, I would like to ask everyone to convey their best wishes and words of gratitude to US president Mr Trump,” Putin said.
The talks come as the grinding war saw increasing civilian deaths and attacks this summer. Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine.
The war, launched by Russia in 2022, has killed hundreds of thousands and displaced millions.
Russian strikes on Ukraine Saturday killed at least seven people, including in the Kyiv suburbs, Ukrainian officials said.
The Kremlin said it would not strike Kyiv from midnight Saturday, while the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he would halt strikes on Moscow “from now” until Monday.
“The Russian president, the commander-in-chief, has given the order from midnight tonight not to strike Kyiv for three days,” the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said.
Zelenskyy, who had offered a truce during the US visits, later said he had spoken to the US envoys and also promised Kyiv would not strike Moscow.
“From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow,” he said on social media.
The Ukrainian leader said he had spoken to the US officials and that he expected them in Kyiv Sunday.
Russia had earlier struck Kyiv suburbs, with Zelenskyy accusing Moscow of trying to disrupt their visit with overnight attacks on Kyiv’s two airports – as well as on civilian targets in the Dnipro region that killed five people.
“Two people were killed in the Bucha district” outside Kyiv, the head of the Kyiv region, Tymur Tkachenko, said.
Large gaps remain between Russia and Ukraine on how to end the war. On Friday, the Kremlin said it was sticking by the position Putin set out two years earlier – that Ukraine should give up four regions claimed by Russia and not join Nato. That position is intolerable to Ukraine.
Witkoff and Kushner were expected to visit Kyiv on Sunday, which would be the first time the two envoys have visited the Ukrainian capital. Both have visited Moscow before, most recently in January when they met Putin in the Kremlin.
As peace efforts floundered in recent months, with US attention turned to its war with Iran, the conflict has intensified.
Ground troops have been locked in a grinding stalemate along the 775-mile (1,250km) frontline with little advances on either side. Both sides have intensified their aerial attacks in recent weeks, hitting increasingly distant targets.
Ukraine has carried out long-range strikes on Russian military facilities, oil refineries and e-commerce warehouses, to try to degrade Russia’s war effort and economy. Its strikes on Russian oil refineries have led to fuel shortages and rising prices at the pump.
On Friday, a Russian drone hit the headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU), one of the agencies responsible for carrying out deep-strike operations in Russia. Zelenskyy has vowed to retaliate. Russia has also increased its attacks on Kyiv and other cities with waves of bombardments, stretching Ukraine’s air defence systems.
Zelenskyy accused Russia of trying to disrupt the envoys’ visit to Ukraine with strikes on Kyiv’s two airports overnight. “Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X. 
 Officials visiting Ukraine have largely done so by train, as Ukrainian airspace has been closed since 2022 due to the war.
On Friday, Russia carried out overnight strikes, killing five people and wounding five more at a factory in the southern Dnipropetrovsk region, according to the local military administration head, Oleksandr Hanzha. He said those killed were employees working at the factory who were “doing their job when enemy missiles cut off their lives.”
A 62-year-old man was injured and several homes and a building were damaged in another attack on the region’s Nikopol district, Hanzha said.
Russia also struck a shopping centre in the southern Mykolaiv region with drones overnight, damaging the building and injuring a 72-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl. Emergency services said they were repeatedly forced to withdraw because of the threat of more strikes.
Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched ballistic missiles and 167 drones overnight, including jet-powered UAVs. Ukrainian air defences disabled 128 of the drones, the air force said.
Russia’s defence ministry said it had shot down 53 Ukrainian drones overnight.
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin began talks in Moscow with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff regarding a new proposal from US President Donald Trump to end the war in Ukraine. Ahead of the envoys' expected visit to Kyiv, both Russia and Ukraine agreed to a three-day halt on strikes against each other's capitals. Despite the diplomatic efforts, significant gaps remain between the warring nations, with Russia demanding Ukraine cede territory and abandon NATO aspirations.
key_points: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin to discuss a proposal to end the war.
Russia and Ukraine agreed to refrain from striking each other's capitals for three days during the negotiations.
Kushner and Witkoff are scheduled to visit Kyiv on Sunday for their first trip to the Ukrainian capital.
The Kremlin maintains its position that Ukraine must give up four claimed regions and not join NATO, terms rejected by Ukraine.

title: US hits three Iranian oil tankers after saying its warships were targeted
author: Grace Eliza Goodwin
content:
US Central Command released footage of the strikes on Iran-linked tankers
- Published
The US military says it has hit three Iran-linked oil tankers after Iran launched ballistic missiles towards two American Navy warships in the region.
US Central Command (Centcom) said on Saturday it had "permanently disabled" a tanker near Kharg Island and another near Jask in the Gulf of Oman, and "completely destroyed" a third in the Gulf of Oman.
"It's simple: if Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers," Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on social media.
Iranian state media confirmed that US forces struck three of its oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island.
Kharg Island is a small rocky outcrop just 15 nautical miles (24km) off the coast of Iran. Ninety percent of Iran's crude oil comes through a terminal on the island - transported through pipes from the mainland.
Iranian state media outlet IRIB reported that there were no casualties in the attack on the tanker near Kharg Island, and that footage indicates the vessel's cooling system put out the fire within an hour.
The crews aboard the two attacked tankers in the Gulf of Oman were taken to shore in lifeboats, IRIB reported. One of those tankers was empty and the other was carrying a load of oil, it added.
Tehran did not immediately acknowledge Iranian attacks on US ships.
Centcom said it "successfully evaded" multiple attacks from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeting a US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer. No American troops were harmed, it said.
Admiral Brad Cooper, Centcom's commander, said in a statement on Saturday: "Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost - taking out three of yours."
"We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet."
Centcom, which oversees US military operations in the Middle East, claimed that the three Iranian oil tankers were "part of a multi-billion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies".
The strikes come nearly a week after renewed attacks between the US and Iran, which followed a period of relative calm between the warring sides.
The US resumed attacks on Sunday, when it said it had struck two rocket launchers to prevent them being used to lay naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
On Tuesday, President Donald Trump said the US had launched a further "very heavy attack", but claimed the renewed fighting would not last "too long".
The strikes prompted Iran to retaliate against US targets in the region, including in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan.
On Thursday, US Vice-President JD Vance also addressed claims by Iran that American strikes killed at least four people, including two children, at a wedding in southern Iran. He said he was "extremely sceptical" over reports of the alleged strike, but confirmed the US would investigate.
Humanitarian group the Iranian Red Crescent Society said shrapnel from a missile hit the ceremony at a home in Sirik on Tuesday, prompting Tehran to declare it a "war crime".
A 60-day ceasefire between the US and Iran formally expired last month, with little sign of a further diplomatic settlement on the horizon.
Days after the ceasefire expired, Trump said the US would launch tougher economic measures against Iran, as well as any country that helps or does business with it.
The US and Israel first launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic.
The Strait of Hormuz previously served as one of the busiest oil-shipping routes, carrying about 20% of the world's oil and LNG supplies.
Currently, the strait has become a major point of conflict between Iran and the United States, with Iran seeking greater control over the waterway and threatening a crucial global trade route.
The conflict in the strait has raised energy prices globally. And, ahead of the US midterm elections in November, Trump is facing pressure over how much the war is costing American consumers.
On Friday, the average price for one gallon of diesel in the US hit $5.85, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago and above the previous high following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA).
- ![Large ships in the Strait of Hormuz are visible near the beach of Bandar Abbas.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/baab/live/f7f345a0-a4b4-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
- ![Split screen. Left, Iran war amongst the rubble. Right, Donald Trump is seen.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/0d95/live/dc3d5fe0-a24c-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
  - Published3 days ago
 ![A handout picture made available by the Iranian Red Crescent Society reportedly showing a view of the destroyed remains of a building which was hosting a wedding ceremony following a US airstrike, in the city of Sirak, Bandar Abbas province, southern Iran, 02 September 2026.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/719/cpsprodpb/3f37/live/8eb97870-a6e4-11f1-9e4c-79c1c0e340c6.jpg)
summary: The US military struck three Iran-linked oil tankers after Iran launched ballistic missiles at two American Navy warships in the region. US Central Command reported that the strikes permanently disabled or destroyed the vessels, which are allegedly part of a shadow network funding the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. No American troops were harmed in the attempted attack on US ships. The military actions follow the expiration of a 60-day ceasefire last month, escalating conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and driving up global energy prices.
key_points: The US military hit three Iran-linked oil tankers after ballistic missiles were targeted at two American warships.
US Central Command stated that the tankers were part of a shadow network funding the IRGC and regional proxies.
Iranian state media confirmed the strikes on three oil tankers, noting no casualties on the Kharg Island vessel and safe evacuation of crews in the Gulf of Oman.
The ongoing conflict follows the expiration of a 60-day ceasefire, causing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and rising fuel prices globally.

title: Putin signs off on 72-hour ceasefire with Kyiv as US envoys visit
author: Mathieu Pollet
content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv as U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow hoping to restart stalled negotiations to end the war in Ukraine.
Kyiv had previously proposed a ceasefire ahead of the diplomatic talks.
“Indeed, such information was received from the Ukrainian side. Russian President and Commander-in-Chief Putin gave orders to hold off on attacks on Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight today,” Moscow press secretary Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media on Saturday.
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered a 72-hour halt to strikes on Kyiv following a proposal from Ukraine. The ceasefire announcement coincided with the arrival of U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow to revive stalled peace negotiations. Kremlin press secretary Dmitry Peskov confirmed the order, which began at midnight.
key_points: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv.
The ceasefire began at midnight following a proposal previously made by Ukraine.
U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow during the ceasefire.
The diplomatic visit and ceasefire aim to restart stalled negotiations to end the war.

title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flood disaster
author: William Christou
content:
Emergency responders rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations on Saturday, as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.
The Nepali military said a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.
Rescue efforts have focused on a dozen hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing, 500 of whom are thought to be trapped in huge tunnels. International rescue teams from India, China, South Korea and the US have been searching through debris and damaged structures at the projects to try to find survivors.
Two Nepali workers were rescued from another tunnel in a hydro-station on the Trishuli River on Friday.
Experts have said that as time passes, the possibility of finding missing people alive in the tunnels is diminishing.
The Nepali woman, 64, was rescued from a damaged house in the devastated town of Nuwakot. Photos published by the Nepali army showed rescuers discovering the woman submerged in mud before she was pulled to safety and airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment. 
 Members of Nepal’s police force cheered as she was pulled from the home, the lower half of which was buried in thick sludge.
Emergency responders have been working to find survivors from the devastating floods in Nepal, which were triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on 26 August. Their work has been complicated by the massive infrastructural damage caused by the floods, with more than 40 bridges having collapsed and rivers swelling unpredictably.
At least 1,375 people have been killed in the floods, with more than 5,000 missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.
summary: Emergency responders in Nepal successfully rescued a Chinese man from a hydropower project tunnel and a 64-year-old Nepali woman from a mud-buried house in Nuwakot. The rescues occurred 10 days after massive floods, triggered by an August 26 glacial and rock collapse, killed at least 1,375 people and left thousands missing. International and local rescue teams continue searching through damaged infrastructure and hydro-station tunnels, though experts warn that the chances of finding more survivors are diminishing.
key_points: A Chinese man was rescued from a tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project by the Nepali military and South Korean disaster experts.
A 64-year-old Nepali woman was rescued from a damaged, mud-buried house in Nuwakot and airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment.
Floods triggered by an August 26 glacial and rock collapse have resulted in at least 1,375 deaths and left over 5,000 people missing.
Rescue operations are focusing on a dozen hydropower projects where about 900 workers remain missing, with around 500 believed trapped in tunnels.
Efforts by international and local rescue teams have been hindered by severe infrastructural damage, including more than 40 collapsed bridges.

title: Judge declares mistrial in Lindsay Clancy murder case as jury deadlocks
author: Ione Wells; Ana Faguy; Sareen Habeshian
content:
Inside court as judge declares a mistrial in Lindsay Clancy case
- Published
Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicide
A Massachusetts judge has declared a mistrial in the murder case against Lindsay Clancy after jurors conceded they would not be able to unanimously decide whether she should be held criminally liable for killing her three young children after a week of deliberating.
The case against Clancy has both captivated and heavily divided the American public, even spurring remarks from the US president.
There was a sense of disbelief in the courtroom as the case - and Clancy's future - were left in limbo.
Clancy's lawyer led a dramatic last-ditch attempt to halt the mistrial and force a verdict, which was unsuccessful. A hearing later this month could establish what happens next in the case.
"At this point, I'm going to declare that the jury is deadlocked and I'm going to declare a mistrial," Judge William Sullivan told the jury on Friday, dismissing them after weeks of testimony, seven days mulling Clancy's fate and the panel signalling three times that they were deadlocked.
The deadlock - known as a hung jury - does not mean prosecutors have proven their case, nor does it mean the defendant is not guilty.
A hearing was scheduled for 29 September, in which prosecutors could outline their next steps in the case.
Meanwhile, the 36-year-old former nurse will remain held on the same murder charges and continue to stay in the mental health facility in which she is currently housed.
Prosecutors could decide from a host of options as to what happens next, including holding another trial or coming to a plea agreement with Clancy over the strangulation of her children - five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan - in their Massachusetts home.
After killing the children, Clancy cut herself âwith a knife and jumped from a second-story window in an attempt to take her own life, which left her paralysed.
Clancy does not deny killing the children in 2023 but pleaded not guilty to the three first-degree murder charges, with her lawyers arguing she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and so should not be held criminally responsible.
![Clancy family picture exhibited in court](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/c476/live/f45d9640-a629-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
A photo displayed in court shows Clancy, her ex-husband and their children
The grim case led to a series of dramatic twists and turns as the jury deliberated Clancy's fate.
On Friday, a court session began with Clancy's attorney Kevin Reddington pushing for a juror on the panel to be removed, after the jury indicated a day prior in a note that a member of the panel had not been following instructions on reasonable doubt.
Under US law, a jury must unanimously believe "beyond a reasonable doubt" that someone is guilty to convict them of a crime.
The designation is the strictest standard in the US legal system. It places the burden on the government to prove that the accused is guilty, instead of the accused to prove their innocence.
The judge denied the request and sent jurors back to deliberate. About an hour later, the panel came back to say they still could not reach a verdict.
It was then that Sullivan said he had no choice but to declare a mistrial. Reddington immediately pleaded for a temporary pause so they could file an emergency appeal with the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court.
Watch: What is a mistrial and what does it mean for Lindsay Clancy?
In the filing, Reddington asked the state's highest court to order the judge to force the jury to continue deliberating and for the judge to question the panel over the alleged holdout juror that led to the deadlock.
The state's high court denied the request, paving the way for the mistrial.
Clancy appeared downcast as the judge made the ruling official. It was surprisingly quiet in courtroom.
She remained expressionless but her lawyer looked visibly upset by the decision. He continued to push back, insisting the judge had the power to dismiss the one holdout juror.
"Unfortunately, they're not holding out based on a good-faith issue," he said.
Reddington said he intended to file another motion essentially requesting that the mistrial be reconsidered. This could come up at the next hearing later this month.
How the Lindsay Clancy trial gripped America - and ultimately fell apart
"There will be no decisions made today," Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz said on Friday concerning what could happen next in the case.
He said he would meet the rest of their legal team to decide whether they would pursue a new trial.
"The facts are Lindsay Clancy killed her three children and the evidence suggested to us that she was in control of her actions when she committed those homicides," Cruz said.
Outside the court on Friday, Reddington said he believed 11 of the 12 jurors would have delivered a verdict that favoured Clancy had it not been for the one holdout.
But it remains unclear what position any member of the jury took or what occurred in the deliberation room.
For weeks, the case gripped the country and sparked debate over the topic of postpartum psychosis. Many followed along with livestreams of the trial, as family members and experts testified. Each day, more than 200 members of the media crowded the court and groups of supporters in varying sizes often gathered outside.
The widespread attention even spurred comments on Friday from US President Donald Trump, who called the case a "horrible tragedy".
"She did a horrible, horrible thing. Can't be worse," he said. "I assume there's going to be another trial."
Trump added: "But you'll find out what the price to pay is. There'll be a price."
If you are suffering distress or despair and need support, you could speak to a health professional, or an organisation that offers support. Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide, external. www.befrienders.org.
A list of UK organisations that can help is available here.
- ![Lindsay Clancy on the stand](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/997/cpsprodpb/38e3/live/56feb170-91e0-11f1-9bc8-c9e5b4077192.jpg)
  - Published16 hours ago
 ![Kevin Reddington sits in court in Plymouth, Massachusetts on 17 August](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/3544/live/77fa7f80-a888-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
summary: A Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in the murder case against Lindsay Clancy after the jury deadlocked following seven days of deliberations. Clancy does not deny killing her three children in 2023, but her defense argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and should not be held criminally responsible. Prosecutors will determine their next steps, which could include a new trial or a plea agreement, at a hearing scheduled for September 29.
key_points: A judge declared a mistrial after the jury deadlocked and could not reach a unanimous verdict after a week of deliberations.
Clancy pleaded not guilty to three first-degree murder charges for the 2023 deaths of her children, with her defense arguing she suffered from postpartum psychosis.
Clancy remains held on murder charges and will continue to stay in a mental health facility.
A hearing is scheduled for September 29 to determine the next steps for prosecutors, which may include holding another trial or pursuing a plea agreement.

title: Witkoff and Kushner will travel to ‘end’ Russia’s war in Ukraine: Trump
author: Evan Semones
content:
![US President Donald Trump speaks before signing executive orders releated to beef processing and cattle ranchers, in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on September 4, 2026. (Photo by Kent NISHIMURA / AFP)](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/afp_6a9b20f0e9ec-1788551408.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
United States President Donald Trump said that US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are travelling this weekend in an attempt to revive peace talks between Ukraine and Russia.
On Friday, while speaking at the White House, Trump said Witkoff and his son-in-law Kushner, who are preparing to travel to Kyiv and Moscow this weekend, are bringing a proposal to “end the war”.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Ten injured in Ukraine as Kyiv expects talks with US envoys in coming days
- list 2 of 3US envoys headed to Russia and Ukraine to relaunch mediation
- list 3 of 3Russian drone strikes Ukraine’s security service headquarters
“I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner … to see whether or not we can get something done,” Trump said. “And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it.”
“We have an idea for peace,” Trump added without mentioning any specifics about his administration’s plan.
According to Russian state news agency TASS, Witkoff and Kushner will be in Moscow on Saturday and Sunday, their first visit since January.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also said the duo would be in Ukraine on Sunday, marking their first visit to the country since Trump returned to power.
Russian President Vladimir Putin recently said negotiations were “frozen”. But this weekend’s expected talks come as both sides continue to ramp up air attacks, with Russia hitting the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security services on Friday.
At least 12 people were injured in the strike, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine, reporting from Kyiv, said that while people weren’t shocked the SBU building was hit, it has made them wonder what target might be next.
“It’s not so much that people never expected the SBU to be hit, but it really raises the question of if Russia can hit this, what else can it hit?” she said. “Some people here are wondering whether this attack, for example, could be aimed at possibly dissuading” the US envoys’ trips to Ukraine.
Trump told reporters Friday that a peace deal in the more than four-year conflict has remained elusive due to what he described as a “personality problem” between both sides.
“President Zelenskyy and President Putin truly hate each other,” Trump said. “They have serious hate, and it’s getting in the way.”
While exact figures are unknown, a study released in July by the Center for Strategic and International Studies says the war has cost Russia some 450,000 lives. Ukraine is estimated to have endured between 125,000 and 150,000 fatalities.
summary: US President Donald Trump announced that US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Kyiv and Moscow to revive peace talks and propose a plan to end the Russia-Ukraine war. The weekend visit marks the envoys' first trip to both countries since Trump returned to power, coming amid ongoing air attacks and a recent Russian strike on Ukraine's security service headquarters. Trump attributed the difficulty in reaching a peace deal partly to a severe personal animosity between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
key_points: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Kyiv and Moscow to attempt to relaunch peace negotiations.
President Donald Trump stated the envoys are bringing a proposal to end the war, though specific details were not disclosed.
The diplomatic visit coincides with intensified air attacks, including a Russian strike on Ukraine's SBU security service headquarters in Kyiv that injured at least 12 people.
Trump cited a deep personal hatred between Presidents Zelenskyy and Putin as a major obstacle that has kept a peace deal elusive.

title: Trump's peace envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv over weekend
author: Jaroslav Lukiv
content:
![US negotiators Jared Kushner (left) and Steve Witkoff. Photo: April 2026](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/0e39/live/bcf0df00-a86d-11f1-bbad-43eaf67b94b6.jpg)
Jared Kushner, Donald Trump's son-in-law (left), and Steve Witkoff are expected to hold separate meetings with the presidents of Russia and Ukraine
- Published
US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia and Ukraine this weekend, as efforts to end the war appear to be gathering pace.
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed he will meet the envoys on Sunday, after they visit Moscow on Saturday to hold talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Witkoff and Kushner have led US President Donald Trump's efforts to broker a peace deal, but a gulf remains between the two warring sides.
"They are bringing with them a proposal to end the war," Trump told reporters when asked about the visits.
Earlier on Friday, Zelensky said a Russian drone hit the office of Ukraine's security chief Oleksandr Poklad in Kyiv. Poklad appears to be unharmed.
In a post on social media, Zelensky said he had ordered Poklad, who head the SBU security service, to respond "adequately" to the attack.
Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Russia multiple times, but the purported talks will be the first in Ukraine.
Zelensky said he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys' visit and called for Russia to do the same for Ukraine.
Russia's state news agency Tass said Witkoff and Kushner were "expected to arrive in Moscow and then to Kyiv... on 5-6 September", quoting a source.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later told reporters: "I wouldn't announce anything, but when these contacts take place, we will inform you."
Meanwhile, Putin told an international economic forum on Thursday that "there are chances" a peace deal could be reached.
"First of all, Moscow and Kyiv must agree between themselves," he said.
But he showed no sign of backing down from his maximalist demands, which included more territorial concessions from Ukraine.
Kyiv and its European allies have repeatedly rejected Putin's terms saying they are tantamount to capitulation.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and currently controls about 20% of its territory.
